input.question: What's the oldest piece of music we have recreated?
input.ground_truth: Recently the Lyre Ensemble has done a whole album recreating songs based on Mesopotamian texts from about 4000bc. [Here](_URL_2_) is the Newsweek article about it and [here](_URL_2_) is the Lyre Ensemble's website with some of the songs from the album.

response.prediction: Okay! Imagine you have a really, really old toy. The oldest toy you can find is maybe 100 years old. But music is even older! People have found ways to write down old songs that are more than 4,000 years old. The oldest music we can play today is from ancient times, like from when people lived in big houses made of mud bricks, called the Egyptian pyramids time! We found some marks on old clay tablets that tell us how to play the music. We learned how to play it using special instruments, like really old flutes. So, the oldest music we can actually listen to today is over 4,000 years old!
